entries.name: Available to promise
entries.purpose: The stock LN will still promise to a new order, worked out over time, and the second check on components and capacity that follows when that stock falls short.

entries.name: Backorder
entries.purpose: The part of a sales order line that the final delivery did not ship, which waits to be confirmed and then becomes a new line to deliver.

entries.name: Business partner
entries.purpose: Any party you trade with, where customer and supplier are two roles on one partner and not two separate records.

entries.name: Contract deliverable
entries.purpose: A second way to raise demand on an item, beside a sales order, which planning ignores until it is switched on and whose supply stays tied to its project.

entries.name: Order planning
entries.purpose: LN's name for what most people call MRP. It lives in the package called Enterprise Planning, beside master planning, which is LN's name for MPS.

entries.name: Order type
entries.purpose: A code on an order that carries the procedure the order will follow, so changing it changes how the same order behaves.

entries.name: Planned order
entries.purpose: Planning's proposal to buy or make something, which becomes a real order only when it is transferred and can be thrown away until then.

entries.name: Release
entries.purpose: LN's verb for handing an order from one module to the next. It changes a status and unblocks the next step, and it moves no goods.

entries.name: Scenario
entries.purpose: One complete planning answer. Every planning screen is scoped by one, and only the actual scenario is real.

entries.name: Session
entries.purpose: Infor's word for a screen. Each has a code, shown in the status bar, that names it exactly.

entries.name: Shipment and load
entries.purpose: What leaves the warehouse together. LN groups picked lines into a shipment and shipments into a load by itself, and reads each one's status from the lines under it.

entries.name: Site and warehouse
entries.purpose: Four things often heard as one: a warehouse is where goods are, a site where a business is, an enterprise unit who accounts for it, and a planning cluster what plans it.

entries.name: Warehousing order
entries.purpose: The order that controls every movement of goods in a warehouse. Most are generated by sales, purchase and production orders, and a transfer is entered by hand.

entries.name: Warehousing procedure
entries.purpose: The list of steps an order takes through the warehouse, each one run by LN or left to you, which is why advice, pick, freeze and confirm do not always apply.

entries.name: WIP
entries.purpose: The value a production order has taken in and not yet delivered. Issuing material or posting hours books it, and the first booking makes the order Active.
